notes: Podcasts work again. Every podcast feed had stopped loading - opening any show reported "No episodes found", on every release from 1.8.8.1 through 1.8.8.5. A security-hardening line called an XML-parser setting Android's built-in parser does not implement, and it threw before a single byte of any feed was read. Faster cold starts. Tarang now ships a baseline profile: a record of the code paths a real launch actually uses, so Android can compile them ahead of time instead of interpreting them on your first run - this helps most on the budget hardware the app is built for. Offline banner tells the truth now. It said "Offline" even when you were online; it now says "Cached" when your connection is fine and the station list is simply due a refresh. On a first launch that never reached the network it read "Updated Jan 1, 1970 ago", and now correctly says "No cached data". Removed: Audio-Coupled Haptics. That switch never actually did anything on any device - Android only routes generated vibration alongside audio if the audio track opts in, and the media library Tarang uses gives no way to ask for that. The ordinary Haptic feedback setting for taps is unaffected. Under the hood. Networking moved to OkHttp 5, which races IPv4 and IPv6 when connecting instead of trying them one after the other - a dead address family now costs a moment rather than a full timeout, the common case on Indian mobile networks.
